_comment: Seed catalog for the discovery-first 'top-library recent-major-release' strategy.
Each entry is a TOP, widely-used, NON-ANDROID, comparatively SIMPLE Maven library that
shipped a RECENT MAJOR release. We mine client repos that upgraded ACROSS the
'boundary' (major.0.0) and adapted -- ideally with test failures / test fixes.
- not Android / not Android-only (okhttp is flagged android_adjacent=true, kept with caveat)
- simple, general-purpose libraries -- avoid frameworks (Spring, Hibernate ORM) whose
- SAME group:artifact across the boundary, so a client's bump is one <version> diff the
traversal detector (bbc_e2e.find_boundary_bump) can actually see. Major releases that
ALSO change the Maven coordinates (jackson 3 -> tools.jackson, rxjava 2->3, httpclient5,
axon/xstream transitive) are recorded under `coordinate_change_majors` and are NOT auto-
detectable as a single-line bump -- listed for reference only.
boundary       = the major.0.0 where the new behaviour lands (client must be < boundary before).
prev_major     = newest pre-boundary line (a sane differential baseline).
java_min       = minimum JDK the NEW major needs (harness hint).
why_simple     = one-line justification it fits the 'simple library' criterion.

libraries.why_simple: test-doubles library; upgrade breaks are localised (inline mock maker default, JDK bump).
logging facade; single-artifact, provider-binding change at 2.0.
YAML parser; 2.0 tightens loading defaults (no global tags / SafeConstructor).
DB migration tool; single concern, well-defined config surface.
Redis client; 5.0 removes deprecated ctors/APIs -- clean surface.
DB driver; 5.0 drops deprecated APIs -- self-contained.
serialization codec; single artifact, numeric 3.x -> 4.x bump.
client library (not the broker); 4.0 removes old protocol/API surface.
in-memory cache; 3.0 just requires Java 11 + minor API cleanups.
JDBC connection pool; 5.0 = Java 11 baseline, tiny API.
office-file library; already a proven break line in this repo's catalog.
HTTP client; runs fine on the JVM but is ALSO an Android staple -> android_adjacent, kept with caveat.

coordinate_change_majors.note: listed for reference; NOT auto-detectable as a single <version> bump because the major ALSO changes the Maven coordinates -- the client removes one dep and adds another.
